PAPERS.title: Significant suppression of sulfur-containing organic aerosols by emission controls during the Hangzhou Asian Games.
PAPERS.short: Hangzhou Asian Games emission controls WSOC FT-ICR MS organosulfate oligomers quasi-natural experiment 2026
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 water-soluble organic carbon by FT-ICR MS before, during and after the Games
PAPERS.endpoint: Molecular composition of sulfur-containing organic aerosol
PAPERS.affil: Beihang University (Hangzhou International Innovation Institute), China; Beihang University, China
PAPERS.n: Quasi-natural experiment around the 19th Asian Games: WSOC in PM2.5 characterised by ultrahigh-resolution FT-ICR MS across control and post-Games periods. Controls coincided with selective depletion of high-molecular-weight organosulfate oligomers (O10-O13) and highly oxygenated CHOS species, consistent with suppressed acid-catalysed oligomerisation and curtailed ageing; Games-period pollution was dominated by humidity-enhanced aqueous processing, the post-Games rebound by gas-phase oxidation yielding organic dinitrates. No PM2.5 mass change, sample count or uncertainty is given in the abstract, and a single event with co-varying meteorology cannot separate control effects from weather. Relevance: indirect - composition shifts of this kind change optical-sensor response per unit mass, a reason not to transfer calibrations across policy regimes.

PAPERS.title: Three-dimensional identification of dominant atmospheric pollutants and their sensitivity to soil moisture in northwestern China urban agglomerations.
PAPERS.short: Urumqi-Changji-Shihezi soil moisture PM2.5 PM10 sensitivity threshold CALIOP aerosol typing 3D
PAPERS.pm: Surface PM2.5 and PM10 against soil moisture; CALIOP aerosol subtypes in 3D
PAPERS.endpoint: Soil-moisture sensitivity thresholds of PM; vertical aerosol-type frequency
PAPERS.affil: Xinjiang Normal University, China; Xinjiang Normal University, China
PAPERS.n: Northwest China urban agglomeration: surface PM2.5 and PM10 related to soil moisture, with CALIOP lidar used to map aerosol subtypes in three dimensions. Sensitivity thresholds of both fractions to soil moisture fell at 0.2266-0.2389 m3/m3 (precipitation effects excluded), PM10 being more sensitive. Moist mountain units showed negative PM-moisture correlation (suppressed dust suspension), dry desert and plain units positive correlation (resuspension). Polluted dust dominated below 4 km, polluted continental aerosol below 2 km, with a stable mixed-dust layer aloft. The abstract does not state the PM data source, period or how thresholds were estimated. Relevance: indirect - dust-dominated regimes are where optical low-cost sensors under-read coarse mass; a moisture threshold is a usable covariate for that correction.

PAPERS.title: PM2.5-induced liver injury mediated by lipid accumulation via the endoplasmic reticulum stress-related IRE1alpha-XBP1s pathway in mice.
PAPERS.short: Central China Normal mouse 12-week PM2.5 liver lipid accumulation IRE1a-XBP1s ER stress inhibitor
PAPERS.pm: PM2.5 exposure of mice for 12 weeks at graded concentrations
PAPERS.endpoint: Hepatic triglyceride synthesis, liver injury, IRE1a-XBP1s pathway proteins
PAPERS.affil: Central China Normal University, China; Central China Normal University, China
PAPERS.n: Mice exposed to PM2.5 for 12 weeks; histopathology, liver-injury markers and proteomics. Lipid accumulation stemmed mainly from triglyceride synthesis; differentially expressed liver proteins clustered in ER processing and fatty-acid metabolism, and IRE1a-XBP1s pathway protein expression rose with PM2.5 concentration. Co-administration of a specific IRE1a-XBP1s inhibitor lowered pathway expression and attenuated both lipid accumulation and liver injury. The abstract gives no exposure concentration, route, particle source or animal numbers, so the dose cannot be placed against human ambient levels, and the inhibitor result supports necessity of the pathway in this model only. Relevance: indirect - adds a hepatic steatosis mechanism to the metabolic arm of PM toxicity; no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: Revealing the contribution of sulfate-containing particles from industrial emissions to atmospheric environment through CCSEM: Insight into morphology, formation, and transport.
PAPERS.short: Steel plant CCSEM 91185 single particles Na2SO4 sulfate near-source sedimentation transport 6-20 km
PAPERS.pm: Individual particles by computer-controlled SEM at five sites inside and around a steel plant
PAPERS.endpoint: Particle type, size and number fraction with distance from source
PAPERS.affil: Chinese Research Academy of Environmental Sciences, China; Institute of Atmospheric Physics, CAS, China
PAPERS.n: CCSEM classified 91,185 individual particles from five sites within a steel plant and its surroundings. By number, Na-rich (46.6%), Ca-rich (21.5%) and Si-rich (8.2%) particles dominated, spanning 0.2-43.6 um. Elongated submicron Na2SO4 particles made up 72.8% of particles nearest the exhaust outlet, aged rapidly (mean size 1.1 to 3.4 um) with 96.2% depositional removal inside the plant, and fell to 5.3% (2.2-11.7%) at ambient sites 6-20 km away. Number fractions are not mass fractions, a single plant and campaign are shown, and the deposition figure is inferred from composition gradients rather than flux measurement. Relevance: indirect - fenceline sensor networks around steel plants will see a size distribution very different from the urban background they were calibrated in.

PAPERS.title: Exposure-response relationships of outdoor and household air pollution with biomarkers of inflammation and oxidative stress in rural Chinese adults.
PAPERS.short: Rural Beijing solid-fuel cohort 1064 adults outdoor household personal PM2.5 black carbon TNF-alpha IL-6 CRP MDA
PAPERS.pm: Village outdoor PM2.5 (continuous), household PM2.5 (~30% subsample), 24-h personal PM2.5 and black carbon
PAPERS.endpoint: Serum IL-6, TNF-alpha, CRP, malondialdehyde
PAPERS.affil: McGill University, Canada; University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, China
PAPERS.n: Longitudinal panel of 1,064 adults (mean age 61) in 50 villages over two heating seasons (2018-19, 2019-20), in a region where residential solid fuel dominates PM2.5. Outdoor PM2.5 was monitored continuously per village, household PM2.5 in about 30% of homes, plus 24-h personal PM2.5 and black carbon; models with individual random effects. TNF-alpha rose 1.9% (95% CI 0.2-3.6%) per 10 ug/m3 outdoor PM2.5; no clear association for household or personal exposure, or with IL-6, CRP or MDA. Household exposure was multiply imputed for ~70% of homes, which biases those estimates toward the null, and four biomarkers by four exposures invites one chance hit. Relevance: direct - one of few cohorts with outdoor, indoor and personal PM side by side; the null for measured personal exposure is the result to watch.

PAPERS.title: Hourly population movement and static-to-dynamic PM2.5 exposure discrepancies in Seoul, South Korea.
PAPERS.short: Seoul 424 dongs hourly PM2.5 surface mobile-network population static vs dynamic exposure discrepancy 2023
PAPERS.pm: Hourly PM2.5 surface estimates weighted by hourly mobile-network population presence
PAPERS.endpoint: Residence-based minus mobility-weighted PM2.5 exposure by hour, neighbourhood type and subgroup
PAPERS.affil: State University of New York at Buffalo, USA; Yonsei University, South Korea
PAPERS.n: All 424 Seoul administrative neighbourhoods in 2023: residence-based daily-mean PM2.5 compared with a place-based estimator weighting hourly concentrations by mobile-network population counts. The citywide mean daily discrepancy was modest but systematic: residence weighting underestimated working-hour exposure in activity hubs and evening/overnight exposure in residential neighbourhoods, while mixed-use areas sat near zero. Discrepancies were larger on weekdays and in winter and spring; working-age adults had the largest gaps in hubs, but winter gaps among youth were 25-51% greater. Seasonal variation reflected PM2.5 levels, not population rhythm. Both inputs are modelled surfaces, and indoor time is ignored. Relevance: direct - hourly sensor networks are what make the place-based estimator possible; daily-mean surfaces discard exactly this signal.

PAPERS.title: The interplay of urban proximity, environmental exposures and health impacts in Spanish cities.
PAPERS.short: Barcelona Granada Palma Valencia 100 m urban proximity index PM2.5 NO2 NDVI HIA attributable mortality quartiles
PAPERS.pm: Gridded PM2.5 and NO2 at 100 m against WHO guideline counterfactual
PAPERS.endpoint: Premature mortality attributable to non-compliance with WHO air quality and greenness guidelines
PAPERS.affil: Yale University, USA; ISGlobal, Spain
PAPERS.n: Four Spanish cities: a 100 m urban proximity index (walkability, cyclability, vitality, 15-minute city) overlaid on PM2.5, NO2, NDVI and population, with grid-level health impact assessment of mortality from non-compliance with WHO guidelines. The most proximate quartile carried the highest burden: PM2.5-attributable mortality 34-102 versus 21-87 per 100,000 in the least proximate, NO2 58-154 versus 20-121, low greenness 21-35 versus 8-17. Ranges span cities; no uncertainty intervals are reported, and applying one concentration-response function across quartiles assumes away the within-city confounding the proximity index carries. Relevance: indirect - central, compact districts are where a 100 m exposure surface most needs dense ground observation to be credible.

PAPERS.title: Association of Ambient Air Pollution Exposure With Early Failure After Incisional Glaucoma Surgery.
PAPERS.short: Fudan three-centre 7820 eyes incisional glaucoma surgery early failure PM2.5 PM10 NO2 O3 CO Cox 2015-2025
PAPERS.pm: Residential geocoded spatiotemporal PM2.5, PM10, NO2, SO2, O3, CO
PAPERS.endpoint: Surgical failure within 30, 60 and 90 days
PAPERS.affil: Eye & ENT Hospital, Fudan University, China; Eye & ENT Hospital, Fudan University, China
PAPERS.n: Three tertiary centres, 7,820 eyes after incisional glaucoma surgery (2015-2025), 466 failures by 30 days, 711 by 60 and 1,083 by 90. PM2.5 was associated with failure at every horizon: adjusted HR 1.090 (1.001-1.187) at 30 days, 1.141 (1.064-1.224) at 60 and 1.240 (1.162-1.324) at 90, roughly linear on splines; O3 and CO mattered early, PM10 and NO2 later, SO2 not at all; no between-centre heterogeneity. The abstract does not state the exposure increment or window, and six pollutants across three horizons with subgroup interactions invite multiplicity. Surgical failure has strong clinical determinants (prior surgery, antimetabolite use) only partly captured. Relevance: peripheral - an unusual endpoint; the exposure is a modelled residential surface.

PAPERS.title: Aerosol-radiation interactions reshape cross-mountain dust transport and downwind air quality responses over a mountain-basin system.
PAPERS.short: Sichuan Basin December 2018 dust intrusion WRF-Chem aerosol-radiation interaction cross-mountain PM10 ozone
PAPERS.pm: PM10 and ozone from multi-source observations and online-coupled WRF-Chem with/without ARI
PAPERS.endpoint: Cross-mountain PM10 flux, near-surface PM10, boundary-layer height
PAPERS.affil: Sichuan University, China; Sichuan University, China
PAPERS.n: One dust intrusion into the Sichuan Basin (2-5 December 2018) analysed with observations, Lagrangian dispersion and WRF-Chem with and without aerosol-radiation interactions. Dust crossed the Qinling-Daba mountains on elevated pathways, raising PM10 and ozone. ARI cut maximum boundary-layer height by 17.5% over the plateau and 28.7% in the basin, lowered cumulative cross-mountain PM10 transport by 13.6% and near-surface basin PM10 by 23.5 ug/m3 (about 10%); ozone rose 8.2 ppbv. A single event and a single model configuration; the ARI effect depends on the dust optical properties assumed. Relevance: indirect - forecasts that omit ARI overpredict basin PM10 during dust events, which matters when they are used to flag sensor outliers.

PAPERS.title: Titanium dioxide exposure in the Western Australian mining industry: Implications for compliance with current and proposed exposure limits.
PAPERS.short: Western Australia mining TiO2 604 personal inhalable samples 2018-2025 proposed ultrafine fine exposure limits
PAPERS.pm: Personal inhalable TiO2 samples from the state regulator's database
PAPERS.endpoint: Exceedance of current (10 mg/m3) and proposed (0.3, 2.4 mg/m3) TiO2 limits
PAPERS.affil: Edith Cowan University, Australia; Edith Cowan University, Australia
PAPERS.n: De-identified regulator data: 604 personal inhalable TiO2 samples from Western Australian mining, 2018-2025, compared with the current 10 mg/m3 inhalable limit and proposed limits of 0.3 mg/m3 (ultrafine/nanoscale) and 2.4 mg/m3 (fine, respirable). Exposures were consistently low; one sample exceeded the numerical value of the proposed ultrafine limit and the second highest was 0.12 mg/m3; none exceeded 2.4 mg/m3; trends were stable or falling. The weakness is the conclusion itself: inhalable gravimetric mass says nothing about the ultrafine/nanoscale fraction the 0.3 mg/m3 limit targets, so 'conservative evidence of compliance' does not follow for that limit. Relevance: peripheral - illustrates why size-specific limits need size-resolved measurement, not legacy inhalable samples.

PAPERS.title: Associations between air pollution, accelerated biological aging, and oral inflammatory diseases: evidence from the UK Biobank cohort.
PAPERS.short: UK Biobank 348247 PM2.5 PM10 PM2.5-10 absorbance NO2 oral inflammatory disease KDM-BA PhenoAge mediation
PAPERS.pm: Residential LUR PM2.5, PM10, PM2.5-10, PM2.5 absorbance, NO2, NOx (2010)
PAPERS.endpoint: Incident oral inflammatory diseases; biological-age acceleration as mediator
PAPERS.affil: Central Hospital of Wuhan, Huazhong University of Science and Technology, China; Gannan Medical University, China
PAPERS.n: UK Biobank, 348,247 adults, median follow-up 16.49 years, 3,967 incident oral inflammatory diseases. Per SD increment, PM2.5, PM10, PM2.5-10 and PM2.5 absorbance were associated with 8%, 4%, 3% and 5% higher incidence (NO2 10%, NOx 8%; all p<0.05). PhenoAge acceleration mediated 8.52-16.65% of the associations, KDM biological age 1.21-5.42%. The abstract reports no confidence intervals. Exposure is a single-year (2010) land-use regression surface applied over 16 years, the outcome comes from hospital coding of a condition mostly managed in primary dental care, and mediation by a biomarker measured at baseline alongside exposure cannot establish temporal ordering. Relevance: peripheral - modelled exposure, no measurement content.

PAPERS.title: ExposomeMap-PM: fine and ultrafine particle-induced toxicity - from adverse outcome pathways to systems biomedicine disease models.
PAPERS.short: Luxembourg Institute of Health ExposomeMap-PM disease map 304 entities 497 processes AOP transcriptomic overlay
PAPERS.pm: Fine and ultrafine particle exposure (knowledge model); one reference particle, 3-day exposure for the overlay
PAPERS.endpoint: Mechanistic network coverage; enrichment of differentially expressed genes
PAPERS.affil: Luxembourg Institute of Health, Luxembourg; Luxembourg Institute of Health, Luxembourg
PAPERS.n: A curated mechanistic disease map linking fine and ultrafine particle exposure to outcomes: 304 entities and 497 processes in five blocks (alveolar deposition, oxidative stress, barrier disruption, mitochondrial dysfunction, pro-inflammatory signalling) ending in asthma, COPD, atherosclerosis and neurodegeneration, built in SBGN and served on MINERVA. In a test overlay from one reference particle and a 3-day exposure, map nodes captured 1.50-fold more differentially expressed transcripts than size-matched random gene sets (permutation p=0.0074); proteomics 1.13-fold. One particle type and a short exposure validate coverage, not completeness, and enrichment is partly guaranteed by curating from the same literature. Relevance: indirect - a reusable scaffold for attaching composition-resolved exposure, which low-cost mass sensors do not provide.

PAPERS.title: Toxic synergy between wood combustion smoke components and high energy visible light on retinal pigment epithelial cells.
PAPERS.short: Laval retinal pigment epithelium wood smoke extract high-energy visible blue light synergy Nrf2 oxidative stress
PAPERS.pm: Wood combustion smoke extract with high-energy visible light co-exposure
PAPERS.endpoint: RPE cell viability, oxidative stress, Nrf2 activation
PAPERS.affil: CHU de Quebec - Universite Laval, Canada; CHU de Quebec - Universite Laval, Canada
PAPERS.n: Human retinal pigment epithelium cells co-exposed to wood combustion smoke extract and high-energy visible (blue) light. The two acted synergistically to reduce viability through oxidative stress that antioxidant treatment mitigated, implying light-sensitive chromophores among smoke constituents; cells activated Nrf2 detoxification. No doses, extract preparation, or how smoke components would reach the retina in vivo are given in the abstract, and an extract is not deposited particulate matter. The plausible exposure path is ocular surface contact or systemic translocation, neither of which the design addresses; the result is a hazard signal for heavy wood-smoke settings rather than an ambient effect. Relevance: peripheral - extends wood-smoke toxicity to a photosensitisation route; no exposure-measurement content.

PAPERS.title: The acoustic environment is structured more by place and fine particulate matter more by time across Rhode Island communities
PAPERS.short: Brown Rhode Island 144 sites 531 site-sessions PM2.5 sound night-time illuminance variance place vs time
PAPERS.pm: Short-session PM2.5 measured at 144 sites, day and night, over 39 days
PAPERS.endpoint: Variance partition of PM2.5 and sound between sites and days; predictors
PAPERS.affil: Brown University, USA; Brown University, USA
PAPERS.n: Preprint. PM2.5, sound and night-time illuminance measured at 144 sites in eight Rhode Island municipalities, four day/night session types over 39 days (531 site-sessions). Sound and PM2.5 were uncorrelated and had different predictors: sound rose near industrial land and varied mainly between sites; PM2.5 tracked weather (falling with wind, rising with temperature and precipitation) and varied mainly between days, rising at night. Results held under penalised regression and spatial-cluster adjustment. The instrument is not named, and short sessions at one site per visit confound site with day, which is exactly the decomposition being estimated. Relevance: direct - quantifies how little between-site PM2.5 contrast short mobile campaigns resolve against day-to-day variance.

PAPERS.title: Machine Learning-Enhanced Air Quality Management via QFIELD and QGIS: Mapping and Bio-cover Materials at Ojota Landfill
PAPERS.short: Ojota landfill Lagos bio-cover QFIELD QGIS PM2.5 PM10 SO2 CO six ML methods AQI risk surface
PAPERS.pm: Point PM2.5 and PM10 at six sampling points 15 m apart, interpolated by ML
PAPERS.endpoint: AQI classification and pollutant risk surface; microbial indicators after bio-cover
PAPERS.affil: Yaba College of Technology, Nigeria; Yaba College of Technology, Nigeria
PAPERS.n: Preprint. Six geo-referenced sampling points at 15 m spacing across the Ojota landfill, Lagos, measuring PM2.5, PM10, SO2 and CO as baseline, then six machine-learning methods (random forest, gradient boosting, SVM, kNN, Gaussian process/regression kriging, ANN) to classify AQI drivers and produce an uncertainty-aware risk surface; a laboratory bio-cover (topsoil, compost, rice husk, earthworm castings) reduced microbial indicators. No PM concentrations, instrument or model skill are reported in the abstract, and six points cannot support six learned spatial models. Relevance: peripheral - shows the demand for landfill-fenceline PM monitoring in West Africa; the analysis is underpowered.

PAPERS.title: LOCATE: Context-Aware GeoAI Decision Support for Population-Oriented Air-Quality Sensor Placement in Data-Constrained Cities
PAPERS.short: AirQo LOCATE GeoAI population-weighted p-median sensor placement Kampala Jinja Nairobi Lagos budgets 5-80
PAPERS.pm: No PM data: siting by modelled residential population plus OpenStreetMap roads and buildings
PAPERS.endpoint: Population-and-context coverage of candidate low-cost sensor layouts
PAPERS.affil: Makerere University / AirQo, Uganda; Makerere University / AirQo, Uganda
PAPERS.n: Preprint from the AirQo group. LOCATE is a pre-deployment siting framework for data-constrained cities that prioritises proximity to modelled residential population while adding road and building context. Six feature-informed clustering methods, two allocation methods and two uninformed baselines were compared across Kampala, Jinja, Nairobi and Lagos for budgets of 5-80 sensors (20 seeds). The context-augmented population-weighted p-median ranked first in all four cities; coverage rose with budget but stayed lower in the larger Lagos and Nairobi domains. The authors state the limitation plainly: layouts are shortlists, not evidence of pollution reconstruction or exposure accuracy, because no concentration field enters the objective. Relevance: direct - siting for low-cost PM networks where no reference surface exists.

PAPERS.title: California petroleum refinery retirements as a natural experiment to assess effects on adverse birth outcomes.
PAPERS.short: UCLA California four refinery retirements difference-in-differences term LBW SGA births 2008-2022
PAPERS.pm: Residential proximity to a retiring petroleum refinery (source proxy; no PM measured)
PAPERS.endpoint: Term low birth weight and small for gestational age
PAPERS.affil: UCLA Fielding School of Public Health, USA; UCLA Fielding School of Public Health, USA
PAPERS.n: Singleton births 2008-2022 conceived within three years before or after the closure of one of four California refineries; difference-in-differences logistic regression, exposed versus unexposed communities by air district. Most retirements were followed by lower odds of term LBW and SGA; strongest for Alon Bakersfield, tLBW OR 0.68 (0.55-0.83) and SGA OR 0.81 (0.74-0.89). Exposure is proximity, not measured PM or any pollutant, so the result cannot be attributed to particles rather than VOCs, SO2 or concurrent economic change; parallel trends across four distinct regions is an assumption the abstract does not test, and the per-refinery heterogeneity is not summarised. Relevance: indirect - fenceline sensor records before and after a closure would supply the exposure contrast this design lacks.

PAPERS.title: PM2.5 Concentrations among Rural Biomass-Fuel and Urban Mixed-Fuel Households in Eastern Ethiopia: A Comparative Cross-Sectional Study
PAPERS.short: Haramaya HDSS 923 kitchens PurpleAir II-SD PM2.5 rural biomass 473 vs urban 80 ug/m3 wet-dry season
PAPERS.pm: Kitchen PM2.5 by PurpleAir II-SD optical sensors, minute data over 3-5 days per household
PAPERS.endpoint: 24-h mean kitchen PM2.5 by residence, season and household factors
PAPERS.affil: Haramaya University, Ethiopia; Haramaya University, Ethiopia
PAPERS.n: Preprint. 923 kitchens (573 rural, 350 urban) in the Haramaya HDSS, eastern Ethiopia, monitored for 3-5 days each with 20 PurpleAir II-SD sensors, January 2023 to December 2024. Mean 24-h PM2.5 was 473 (SD 255) ug/m3 in rural and 80 (92) in urban kitchens, difference 393 ug/m3 (95% CI 370-416). In 96 kitchens measured in both seasons, rural means rose from 343 (dry) to 732 ug/m3 (wet), urban from 47 to 105. All rural homes used open fires. The abstract reports no correction or co-location: uncorrected Plantower readings in dense biomass smoke at high humidity carry large, humidity-dependent bias, which is the same axis as the wet-season contrast. Relevance: direct - the largest low-cost household PM dataset in the Horn of Africa; usable only once a smoke- and RH-specific correction is shown.

PAPERS.title: An OMOP-Compatible Exposure Infrastructure for GeoAI-Enabled Environmental Health Research: The OHDSI GIS Toolchain
PAPERS.short: Tufts OHDSI GIS toolchain OMOP exposure infrastructure synthetic 40000 persons simulated PM2.5 geocoding error attenuation
PAPERS.pm: Geospatial exposure linkage to OMOP CDM; simulated PM2.5 effects on a synthetic cohort
PAPERS.endpoint: Recovery of known exposure effects; attenuation under geocoding displacement
PAPERS.affil: Tufts Clinical and Translational Science Institute, USA; Tufts CTSI, USA
PAPERS.n: Preprint describing an open-source toolchain that standardises geospatial sources into person-place-time exposure records in the OMOP Common Data Model (FAIR catalogue, GIS vocabulary, local geocoding, geometry-attribute index). Tested on a synthetic cohort of 40,000 persons placed in real US census tracts with eight simulated PM2.5 effects and six nulls: derived exposures matched an independent answer key and known effects were recovered. Displacing residences by empirical geocoding error changed estimates little for smooth regional exposure but attenuated them by up to half for exposures varying over 100 m. Synthetic data test plumbing, not real-world exposure validity. Relevance: direct - quantifies why fine-scale (sensor-resolved) surfaces lose half their signal under ordinary geocoding error.

PAPERS.title: Measurement report: Size-resolved seasonal study of inorganic ions and isotopic carbon signatures of aerosol particles at the Wadden Sea
PAPERS.short: Wadden Sea size-resolved inorganic ions levoglucosan 13C 14C organic carbon ship sulfate continental outflow
PAPERS.pm: Size-resolved impactor samples: inorganic ions, levoglucosan, total carbon, 13C and 14C of OC
PAPERS.endpoint: Size-resolved composition and fossil/non-fossil OC by season and wind sector
PAPERS.affil: Not stated; University of Groningen, Netherlands
PAPERS.n: Measurement report from a Wadden Sea coastal site: size-resolved samples by season and wind sector analysed for inorganic ions, levoglucosan, total carbon and stable and radiocarbon isotopes of organic carbon at several desorption temperatures. Land-sector samples were dominated by nitrate, ammonium and total carbon, the single sea-sector set by sulfate and total carbon; sulfate reached 0.5 ug/m3 in both, suggesting ship emissions. Fossil OC fractions were highest below 250 nm (traffic combustion), and 13C signatures pointed to SOA in smaller, more volatile carbon and photochemical processing at larger sizes. One sea-sector sample set limits the ship attribution. Relevance: peripheral - background composition for coastal network sites; no sensing content.

PAPERS.short: IIT Madras operating procedures advanced aerosol instruments high-altitude observatories technical note
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only

PAPERS.short: Cholakian Bertrand northern hemisphere multi-annual concentration exposure simulations analysis

PAPERS.short: Chatoutsidou Lazaridis European major cities mortality burden long-term PM2.5 NO2 updated evidence

PAPERS.short: Jana Delhi road waterlogging post-event PM2.5 satellite-based association robustness road network
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only

No finding is asserted here. Relevance: indirect - a resuspension mechanism that kerbside low-cost networks in Delhi would observe directly; recheck for an abstract.

PAPERS.title: Temporal variations and driving factors of PM2.5 pollution in Wuhan, central China: Insights from water-soluble ions and polar organic compounds
PAPERS.short: Zhang Tang Wuhan PM2.5 temporal variation water-soluble ions polar organic compounds driving factors
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only

PAPERS.short: Thompson Jung airborne microplastic generation transport 3D printing university setting
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only
PAPERS.endpoint: Metadata only
PAPERS.n: Metadata only: no abstract in the Crossref deposit at issue time. Aerosol and Air Quality Research paper on airborne microplastic generation and transport from 3D-printing activities in a university setting. No finding is asserted here. PAPERS.title: Contrasting Dynamics of Particle-Bound Organophosphate Esters Reveal Distinct High-Altitude Contaminant Transport Processes over the Tibetan Plateau
PAPERS.short: Tibetan Plateau QOMS NAMORS particle-bound organophosphate esters PM2.5 warm-season maximum trans-Himalayan transport
PAPERS.pm: Year-round PM2.5 filter samples analysed for organophosphate esters at two sites
PAPERS.endpoint: Particle-bound OPE concentrations, seasonality, source regions
PAPERS.affil: Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, CAS, China; Xizang University, China
PAPERS.n: Year-round synchronous PM2.5 sampling at a southern Himalayan receptor (QOMS) and an inland background site (NAMORS). Sum of OPEs averaged 111 (SD 125) pg/m3 at QOMS and 20 (17) at NAMORS, with a counterintuitive warm-season maximum coinciding with a 72-91% fall in hygroscopic secondary inorganic aerosol, read as trans-Himalayan monsoon transport persisting despite wet deposition. Chlorinated congeners (TCPP, TDCPP) dominated (TCEP/TCPP 0.09-0.46), unlike Arctic profiles; trajectories and PCA point to South Asian sources. The authors note the absence of simultaneous gas-phase data, which leaves partitioning unconstrained. Relevance: peripheral - toxic trace constituents invisible to any mass sensor; remote background context.

PAPERS.title: Unraveling the Effects of Early Life Air Pollution and Temperature Exposure on Children Being Overweight and Obese: Evidence and Intervention
PAPERS.short: Lu Jiang Central South early-life air pollution temperature children overweight obesity evidence intervention
PAPERS.pm: Metadata only

PAPERS.title: Study on the Influence of Personnel Hand Activities in a Cleanroom on the Deposition Characteristics of Released Particulate Matter
PAPERS.short: Xiangtan cleanroom hand activity particle deposition model airflow velocity particle size height
PAPERS.pm: Particles 0.5-10 um released by hand movements; CFD deposition model validated on prior experiments
PAPERS.endpoint: Normalised surface deposition rate by particle size, airflow velocity and hand height
PAPERS.affil: Xiangtan University, China; Xiangtan University, China
PAPERS.n: A particle deposition model for operator hand movements in cleanrooms, checked against existing experimental data and run numerically over hand height, particle size and supply-air velocity. Deposition of 5 and 10 um particles far exceeded that of 0.5-2 um; size differences narrowed with airflow, the 10:5 um deposition-fraction ratio falling from 3.2 at 0.25 m/s to 1.25 at 0.45 m/s; deposition fell sharply up to 0.15 m hand height and slowly above. Inhalation is not modelled despite the occupational framing, and validation data are not described. Relevance: peripheral - near-source coarse-particle deposition; no sensing content.

PAPERS.title: Decision uncertainty in particulate-matter measurement comparability under sparse reference sampling
PAPERS.short: Yangtze 45 US sites 43576 reference-FEM PM2.5 pairs sparse 1-in-3 1-in-6 1-in-12 sampling comparability verdict bootstrap indeterminacy
PAPERS.pm: Daily PM2.5 FRM reference and federal equivalent method pairs, 2022-2025
PAPERS.endpoint: Determinacy of equivalence (slope-intercept) verdicts under thinned reference schedules
PAPERS.affil: Yangtze University, China; Yangtze University, China
PAPERS.n: 45 US sites (2022-2025), 127 episodes, 43,576 same-site reference-equivalent PM2.5 pairs. Each near-daily record was thinned to every phase of 1-in-3, 1-in-6 and 1-in-12 schedules; US equivalence slope-intercept envelopes gave point verdicts, a moving-block bootstrap their stability. 64.6% of near-daily benchmarks were already boundary-uncertain; on the 45 stable episodes, sparse-schedule indeterminacy was 33.0% (21.1-46.1%), 63.8% (53.0-73.8%) and 73.8% (63.7-82.6%), and 88 of 90 point mismatches became indeterminate rather than reversed. In a known-truth 1-in-12 simulation, coverage was about 88% and 14 of 64 stable verdicts had the wrong sign. Single-author-group statistical work, not yet replicated. Relevance: direct - most low-cost sensor 'equivalence' claims rest on sparser reference support than this; report bootstrap state with the verdict.

PAPERS.title: How prenatal residential greenness links to congenital heart defects: The role of multi-pollutant mediating pathways and non-linear exposure-response.
PAPERS.short: Xiamen 890 matched pairs prenatal greenness NDVI landscape indices congenital heart defects NO2 PM2.5 mediation
PAPERS.pm: First-trimester NDVI (250-1000 m) and landscape metrics; NO2, PM2.5, SO2, O3 as mediators
PAPERS.endpoint: Congenital heart defects; indirect effects via air pollutants
PAPERS.affil: Key Laboratory of Urban Environment and Health, CAS, China; Women and Children's Hospital, Xiamen University, China
PAPERS.n: Xiamen birth records 2016-2019: 1,785 CHD cases and 1,848 controls, 890 pairs after 1:1 propensity matching. First-trimester greenness was associated with lower CHD odds; at 1 km, large core patches and connectivity were protective and fragmentation and edge density harmful. Multi-pollutant mediation found indirect paths through NO2 and PM2.5, largest for NO2; the SO2 path did not survive joint modelling and the O3 indirect estimate was positive. The NDVI-NO2 relation turned at NDVI about 0.46. No effect sizes are given in the abstract, the PM2.5 exposure model is not stated, and propensity matching discarded half the cases. Relevance: indirect - PM2.5 enters only as a mediator of greenness.

PAPERS.title: Potential Airborne Particulate Matter (PM) Exposures for Firefighters Working Outside Live-Fire Training Structures.
PAPERS.short: UL FSRI NIOSH live-fire training structures exterior real-time optical PM instructors fuels location
PAPERS.pm: Stationary time-resolved optical real-time PM area measurements outside two live-fire training structures
PAPERS.endpoint: Exterior PM concentrations by fuel load, structure and staging location
PAPERS.affil: Fire Safety Research Institute, UL Research Institutes, USA; NIOSH, USA
PAPERS.n: Stationary optical real-time PM area monitors outside two training structures: a single-storey fire-behaviour lab (five fuels) and a two-storey concrete multicompartment structure (three fuels). In the fire-behaviour lab, fuel load had limited effect on exterior PM, but standing upwind and further from the structure lowered the hazard; at the multicompartment structure fuel load mattered more and the second floor showed high PM where instructors may be unable to relocate. No concentrations, instrument model or smoke-specific correction are given in the abstract; area monitors are not personal breathing-zone exposure. Relevance: indirect - optical monitors in fresh smoke need a smoke-specific mass correction before such numbers are compared with limits.

PAPERS.title: Associations between night-time bedroom environmental factors and objective sleep metrics of older adults.
PAPERS.short: OHSU Portland 29 older adults bedroom PM2.5 light noise temperature humidity TVOC CO2 objective sleep 211 nights
PAPERS.pm: Night-averaged bedroom PM2.5 among seven in-home environmental sensors
PAPERS.endpoint: Total sleep time, WASO, sleep efficiency, movement, heart and respiratory rate
PAPERS.affil: Oregon Health and Science University, USA; Oregon Health and Science University, USA
PAPERS.n: 29 older adults (17 cognitively normal, 12 with MCI or dementia; mean age about 77) followed for a mean 211 nights at home with objective sleep metrics and seven bedroom environmental measures. Light had the strongest association with total sleep time, humidity with WASO and efficiency, temperature with movement and heart and respiratory rate; PM2.5 was associated with total sleep time (effect size -0.050) and sleep efficiency (-0.058), Bonferroni significant. The PM2.5 sensor is not identified, effect sizes are standardised without stated units, and 29 people give many nights but little between-person information. Conference paper. Relevance: direct - long-run in-home PM sensing paired with passive physiology is the deployment model for indoor exposure-response work.
